run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:19:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning fires because frontend-proxy keeps emitting ingress spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR: its Envoy access logs show 5xx responses (500 via_upstream, 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, 504 UT response_timeout) for traffic it proxies to the frontend. The largest observed error burst in the window lines up with the cart Deployment rollout at 2026-11-16T13:22:10Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, generation 2): the single-replica cart Deployment has no readinessProbe, the old cart pod was stopped at 13:22:13 and the replacement cart container only logged its ASP.NET startup line at 13:22:35.9, its first request handling at 13:22:51; frontend-proxy logged 500 via_upstream on /api/cart and /api/checkout from 13:22:14 to 13:22:52, and 186 ingress error spans fall in the minute ending 13:23:40. A second, earlier burst was a 504 response_timeout storm around 13:00 on /api/data, traced as frontend -> ad oteldemo.AdService/GetAds -> flagd ResolveBoolean with a deadline-exceeded error detail. The alert's first crossing at 13:19:40 with value 0.0111 (1/90) matches a single baseline-level 503 UC reset logged at 13:18:27, and similar sporadic 503 UC resets occur before and after the cart burst; their deeper cause is unresolved because frontend and flagd container logs returned no readable lines and Jaeger holds no spans after about 13:08. The RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, so its expression is unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span metrics show STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation "ingress" throughout the window: 50 errors in the minute ending 13:01:40, sporadic 2-4/min until about 13:11, 2 in the minute ending 13:21:40, 186 in the minute ending 13:23:40, and 2-6/min through the minute ending 13:32:40; operation "router frontend egress" shows errors only in the 13:23:40 minute (186).

The 5-minute error increase for frontend-proxy spans was about 105-109 per 5 minutes for the windows ending 13:23:40 through 13:27:40 and then fell, while a separate query shows single-digit 5-minute error increases later (for example 3.82 at 13:33:40), i.e. the error signal persisted at a low level after the burst.

frontend-proxy access logs show 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET /api/data/?contextKeys=assembly at 13:18:27.251 and on GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP at 13:20:27.245, both against upstream "frontend".

frontend-proxy access logs show 500 - via_upstream responses (21-byte bodies) for POST/GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout continuously from 13:22:14.371 to 13:22:52.934, and the 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses reappear at 13:23:27.717, 13:24:33.557, 13:26:46.894 and 13:29:15.559.

The cart Deployment is generation 2 with template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:22:10Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, replicas 1, and both readinessProbe and livenessProbe are null.

Cart rollout events: at 13:22:10 Deployment/cart scaled replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1 and created pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz; at 13:22:13 it stopped container cart of the old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and scaled the old ReplicaSet from 1 to 0.

The new cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz started at 13:22:10; its cart container is running and ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and its image digest matches the unchanged demo 2.1.3-cart image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:84ce75e5...), i.e. a restart/config rollout of the same image rather than a crash or eviction.

The new cart container logged the ASP.NET startup line "Overriding HTTP_PORTS ... Binding to values defined by URLS instead" at 13:22:35.911, about 23 seconds after its 13:22:12 container start, and only from 13:22:51 onward logged normal GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync request handling.
frontend-proxy access logs show 504 UT response_timeout responses of 15001 ms on GET /api/data between 13:00:00.923 and 13:00:26.245.

Traces for those 504s (12:59:48-13:00:34) show frontend GET /api/data server spans of 21.97-45.32 s, frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds of 19.70-45.32 s, ad server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds of 19.70-38.20 s, ad child span resolve of 2.40-12.90 s, flagd flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean error spans with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (11 rows), and one flagd span whose error detail is otel.status_description "context deadline exceeded" with rpc.grpc.status_code=2; the supplied parent references link frontend -> ad -> flagd, and frontend-proxy ingress 504 error spans appear in the same traces.

Checked and healthy at query time: all 21 otel-demo Deployments report 1 ready/available replica, and frontend (pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-64mj8, started 12:51:01), frontend-proxy (pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-v4lvt, started 12:51:02) and valkey-cart (pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-j6cf7, started 12:51:03) have restartCount 0 and no terminated last state; frontend-proxy is also at Deployment generation 1 with no restart annotation.

The frontend service was itself failing during the 13:22 cart burst: a cross-service error-span query evaluated at 13:26:00 (5-minute lookback) returned frontend error spans on GET (25.6), POST (77.8), POST /api/cart (57.8), POST /api/checkout (20), executing api route (pages) /api/cart (83.3), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (57.8), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (25.6) and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (20); this reading is treated as a hypothesis here because the alert rule that produced the 0.0111 ratio is not visible and the exact per-span series for frontend were not re-read.

The alert's first crossing at 13:19:40 with value 0.0111 (1/90) is consistent with a single frontend-proxy error span in the preceding 90 seconds, i.e. the 503 UC reset logged at 13:18:27 (73 s earlier), so the warning fires on essentially any single upstream connection reset. The exact alert expression cannot be confirmed because no rule named RequestErrorRate is loaded in the queried Prometheus.

The 13:22:14-13:22:52 500 burst was caused by the cart rollout handing traffic to a not-yet-listening cart container: with one replica and no readiness probe, the Service endpoint existed as soon as the container started at 13:22:12, while the cart application only began binding at 13:22:35.9, so frontend cart calls failed and the frontend returned 500 pages that frontend-proxy logged as 500 via_upstream.

The recurring 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses (roughly 1-2 per minute, on different paths such as /api/data, /api/products/*, /api/recommendations and /api/cart) originate on the Envoy->frontend connection, for example an upstream keepalive/idle-timeout race or frontend connection termination; this is the error source that kept the frontend-proxy error rate above zero around the alert start and after the cart burst, but the frontend container produced no readable log lines, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.

The ~13:00 504 burst on /api/data was caused by slow flagd flag evaluation (ResolveBoolean context deadline exceeded inside ad.GetAds) rather than by frontend-proxy; the flagd workload is the candidate object, but flagd container logs returned no readable lines so this remains unconfirmed.

frontend-proxy was not restarted, evicted or OOM-killed during the window (restartCount 0, running since 12:51:02, generation 1, no restart annotation), so its error signal reflects upstream responses rather than a crash of the proxy itself.

The separate fraud-detection OOMKill (last state terminated, reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, finishedAt 13:27:40Z, restartCount 1) is not shown to cause the frontend-proxy error rate: frontend-proxy errors were already present before it, including the 503 UC resets at 13:18:27 and 13:20:27 and the 500 burst at 13:22:14-13:22:52, and no fraud-detection evidence ties that container's restart to these responses.

Add a readinessProbe to the cart Deployment and run it with more than one replica and maxUnavailable=0 so a rollout cannot route cart traffic to a container before the ASP.NET application is listening; this would remove the 500 burst observed at 13:22:14-13:22:52.

Review the RequestErrorRate threshold/window for frontend-proxy: it fires above 0 and a single error in 90 s produces 0.0111, so baseline 503 upstream-reset noise alone can keep it firing; require a sustained rate or a minimum error count over a longer window.

Investigate the Envoy->frontend 503 UC connection_termination resets (frontend keepalive settings, Envoy upstream protocol options and idle timeouts, retries for idempotent GETs) and the flagd deadline-exceeded evaluations behind ad.GetAds, and restore log collection for the frontend and flagd containers so both can be confirmed.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data (f40ae078-7d20-4b9c-b1c8-9ffeb8bf33db-t0:828bba1a-26c0-4179-a8df-2072c95d8b2a) and the alert-type listing for {namespace="otel-demo"} returned no_data (459d827a-3077-4c73-aa5e-ff82c869b9e9-t1:6d469c52-c58d-4edb-a74e-9b4c00d853dc), so the alert expression, its window and the meaning of the 0.0111 value are unverified.

Jaeger returned no spans for frontend-proxy between 13:23:00 and 13:29:00 (375ec576-7fe6-4bce-8f1a-3fe1e38f6fbe-t1:3fb9291f-41ad-4d5e-a767-1e2ad64aaf44, status no_data) and none for frontend between 13:24:00 and 13:25:00 (a521e27c-287d-4501-abc3-5b4204dc41b4-t1:8a3c362a-82d0-46d7-b7e0-ca5339921abd) or 13:30:00-13:40:51, so there is no trace evidence for the 13:18-13:30 errors, including the 500 burst and the recurring 503 UC resets.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 13:18-13:32 (db94f97f-6ac0-4559-b7f7-bb747a1c3fc3-t1:f35a16c0-165a-4b51-bcf4-951aea6c872b and bc1518e3-763e-4013-981a-35f89b67c4fd-t0:da5c311e-caf5-4571-9529-f9c8d389d720, both no_data) and the flagd pod's containers returned no readable lines (30ce9cf2-eaf6-4078-bde6-e917ddd9497e-t1:c39e91c6-884e-4741-b199-26ef9285b9e3), so the reason the frontend terminated upstream connections and the reason flagd evaluations hit deadlines could not be read from application logs.

No metrics are available for frontend, flagd or Envoy CPU throttling, connection-pool state or node resources, and the pod and Deployment objects show only current state, so resource-pressure explanations for the 503 UC resets and 504 timeouts remain unverified.

Several reads were capped: the frontend-proxy log reads hit line limits (a521e27c-287d-4501-abc3-5b4204dc41b4-t0:21130d8b-f65c-4906-80cf-bc7002c0ba61, e8952a59-e432-43d8-bb13-c2569a5b6ea4-t1:4bbca64e-0991-4b3a-9cab-2689918c1329, 30ce9cf2-eaf6-4078-bde6-e917ddd9497e-t0:4353486b-fb72-4bc2-895c-e75c81e69480) and one hit the 4 MiB read limit (c7472aae-d6d6-4bac-bb92-24dd0ddc985c-t0:83137388-85c4-44bd-8939-c0acd459f25f), and the 13:00:00-13:00:34 trace search exhausted its requested trace count (f67db6e6-21f0-4152-aaa7-da1c4b8b8b1c-t1:e1ac3e56-10b1-4731-9a13-fc7b7de98849), so additional error lines and traces may exist unread.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the cart rollout (kubectl restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:22:10Z) is evidenced only by the Deployment annotation and Kubernetes events; the previous cart pod and its termination details are no longer observable.
next_steps: Inspect the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source for RequestErrorRate to confirm its PromQL expression, window and threshold, and consider requiring a sustained error rate rather than >0.

Check frontend (Next.js/Node) server keepalive and Envoy upstream protocol options/idle timeouts, and whether retries are configured for idempotent GETs, to explain the roughly 1-2 per minute 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses.
Review flagd resource limits and ad-service evaluation deadlines for the 20-45 s ad.GetAds latency that produced the 13:00 504 timeouts on /api/data.
Fix log collection for the frontend and flagd containers so future investigations can read their application logs.
Add readiness probes and multiple replicas to cart so rollouts do not create a window where the Service sends traffic to a container that is not listening.
